summary: Intercepting egress proxy truncates client cert chain during mTLS to artifact host causing intermittent artifact fetch auth failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's private deploy is failing to download model artifact bundles intermittently. Failures cluster during periods of high parallel artifact fetches and show TLS/mTLS authentication errors from our control plane to the artifact host.

Impact:
- FinSigna production inference jobs intermittently fail to load new model bundles; customers see 5-10% increased model-load latency and a small fraction of requests fail with 401/403 during rollout windows.
- Affects private (VPC) deployment only; hosted customers not impacted.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC, prod-us-east (us-east-1).
- Egress path forced through corporate inline TLS-inspecting proxy that performs certificate rewriting/inspection.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger parallel model rollout that causes 8 concurrent artifact fetches per serving node.
2) Observe artifact fetch logs (control-plane/artifact-fetcher) and TLS negotiation.
3) Failures observed ~30-60s after start of parallel downloads.

Observed behavior:
- Control-plane logs show TLS handshake succeeded but mTLS verification fails at application layer: "client certificate chain incomplete" or "unexpected certificate subject" depending on request.
- Artifact host returns 401 or 403 for the failed fetches.
- Packet captures show the CLIENTHELLO -> PROXY -> UPSTREAM sequence; proxy advertises ALPN and performs active inspection.

Expected behavior:
- mTLS handshake should preserve the full client certificate chain and proof-of-possession so upstream accepts requests.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer's inline proxy is performing TLS interception but truncating part of the client certificate chain or not forwarding the client cert in the upstream mTLS session when connections are multiplexed/HTTP/2 is used. The failure rate increases with concurrency, suggesting a race or connection-reuse edge case in the proxy code.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Nair (Support): Opened ticket after customer reported rollout failures; requested packet captures and control-plane logs.

2026-03-01 FinSigna (Customer): Attached tcpdump from node showing SYN, TLS CLIENTHELLO and a subsequent application-level 401 from artifact host. Customer notes proxy vendor: SecureGate 4.2.1 inline appliance.

2026-03-02 Ethan Park (SRE): Reproduced with a local test harness routing through an interception proxy. Observed truncated certificate chain on upstream connection when HTTP/2 multiplexing was enabled. Filed internal INT-8472 for investigating egress-proxy behavior.
2026-03-03 FinSigna: Confirmed workaround (disable HTTP/2 multiplexing on egress) reduces failure rate to near zero for their rollout tests.
2026-03-04 Engineering (egress-proxy): Created a small test PR to force fresh upstream connections per client cert; waiting review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-proxy/pull/238
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 tcpdump summary from customer: multiple concurrent TLS sessions appear, but upstream server reports 'certificate verify failed: incomplete chain' in app logs.
Checked artifact-fetcher logs: repeated entries 'upstream mTLS verify failed: presenting incomplete client cert chain' correlated with high parallelism windows.

Replicated in lab by deploying SecureGate inline (vendor-supplied VM image) and routing egress through it; when client reuses muxed HTTP/2 stream, proxy establishes upstream TLS separately and fails to attach full client cert chain in 1 of 8 parallel streams.

OpenSSL s_client test: when proxy in-path, s_client -status -alpn h2 -cert client.pem -key client.key -> upstream returns 'verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)' intermittently depending on timing.
Wireshark TLS record inspection shows proxy sending an upstream ClientCertASN1 but missing the intermediate cert in the chain; the downstream (from client to proxy) contains full chain.

Hypothesis: proxy's mTLS passthrough code incorrectly reuses a cached upstream connection which was established without client cert state, then attempts to inject client cert at application layer but loses intermediate CA. Race occurs under high concurrency when proxy opens fresh upstream connections asynchronously.
Related internal reference: INT-8472 (egress-proxy connection-reuse investigation).
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer disabled HTTP/2 connection multiplexing on their egress proxy policy and configured the egress appliance to open dedicated upstream connections per downstream mTLS session. This reduced failures to <0.3% during rollouts.

Permanent fix plan: Engineering to land egress-proxy PR that avoids reusing upstream TLS sessions for connections that require client-certificate propagation and to add a code path ensuring full client certificate chain is forwarded when interception mode is enabled. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-proxy/pull/238 (under review).

Follow-ups:
- Coordinate with customer to test staged rollout of proxy fix next week in a controlled window.
- Add monitoring alert for 'artifact-fetch mTLS verification failure rate' and a knowledge-base article describing recommended egress proxy configs for mTLS-preserving inspection appliances.

Status: Engineering patch pending review; in-contact with SecureGate support to get appliance firmware that properly preserves client certificate chain in interception mode.
